question.problem: A particle $P$ moves along the $x$-axis. When the displacement of $P$ from the origin is $x\,m,$ the velocity is $v\,m/s,$ and the acceleration is $(kx+6)\,{m/s}^{2},$ where $k$ is a positive constant. If $P$ has velocity $v=3\,m/s$ at the origin and the particle has velocity $v=19\,m/s$ when its displacement is $8\,m,$ find the value of $k.$
question.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14273713/assets/f7468aaa11c79f4306b67a558f09cbf5d8a6a480b726e883ecb373d7e5660e37.png)

Since the acceleration of the particle $P$ is $(kx+6)\,{m/s}^{2},$ we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}=kx+6.
$$

Using the fact that

$$
\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}=\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2}),
$$

we can rewrite our equation as

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2})=kx+6.
$$

Integrating both sides of the above equation with respect to $x,$ we have

$$
\int \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2})\text{d}x=\int (kx+6)\,\text{d}x
$$

which gives the general solution

$$
\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2}=\frac{k{x}^{2}}{2}+6x+C.
$$

Now, since $v=3\,m/s$ when $x=0\,m,$ we can find the value of the constant $C,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2} & =\frac{k{x}^{2}}{2}+6x+C \\ \frac{1}{2}(3)^{2} & =\frac{k(0)^{2}}{2}+6(0)+C \\ C & =\frac{9}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2}=\frac{k{x}^{2}}{2}+6x+\frac{9}{2}.
$$

Finally, since $v=19\,m/s$ when $x=8\,m,$ we can find the value of the positive constant $k,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2} & =\frac{k{x}^{2}}{2}+6x+\frac{9}{2} \\ \frac{1}{2}(19)^{2} & =\frac{k(8)^{2}}{2}+6(8)+\frac{9}{2} \\ \frac{361}{2} & =32k+48+\frac{9}{2} \\ 32k & =128 \\ k & =4.\end{aligned}
$$
